sources.entry: browser-use - Make websites accessible for AI agents with easy browser automation.

summary.one_liner: Browser Use is an open-source Python (and TypeScript) browser agent that lets an LLM drive a web browser to complete tasks, with optional hosted cloud browsers and agent API.
summary.what_it_does: The Python library runs a Browser Use agent locally with a chosen LLM (for example ChatOpenAI or ChatBrowserUse) against a local or cloud browser. The Agent takes a natural-language task, opens a browser, and returns a result via history.final_result(). Custom tools can be registered with Tools and an @tools.action decorator. Authentication can reuse a local Chrome profile through Browser.from_system_chrome() or a cloud profile. Runs can be saved to JSON and replayed with new variable values, without a model call per step. The README also describes a Claude toolset integration that uses Browser Use as the browser driver, with a Bash tool included, and a CLI for giving existing coding agents browser access.
use_cases: automate multi-step web tasks with an LLM agent
fill and submit web forms with replayable runs
look up information on websites automatically
run a browser agent in Docker, CI, or serverless via cloud browsers
give Claude or other coding agents browser control
how_to_run: Add OPENAI_API_KEY (or another provider key) to .env
Save the README's agent.py example and run: uv run agent.py
Optional: set BROWSER_USE_API_KEY and use Browser(use_cloud=True) for a cloud browser
notable: Runs with any supported LLM: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, or local models via Ollama, plus the BU2 model via ChatBrowserUse
Same agent code switches between a local browser and Browser Use Cloud with one parameter
Save a successful run and replay its clicks and typing with new variables without per-step model calls
Custom actions registered as plain Python functions with Tools
Claude toolset integration exposing 31 browser actions
caveats: Cloud browsers, hosted agent, and the BU2 model are paid usage ($0.02 per browser-hour plus network traffic, per README), with API keys required
CAPTCHA handling is not guaranteed; the README says no configuration ensures every CAPTCHA can be avoided or solved
Profile sync transfers cookies only, not local storage, IndexedDB, or extensions; some sites may require sign-in again
The Claude Bash tool requires Linux or macOS; Windows users need WSL
